transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Thank you so much for fitting me in, I really appreciate it. Um... I'm not entirely sure how to explain it, and I hope I don't sound silly. But what brings me in is that I’ve just been waking up with this... this heavy, kind of hollow sadness lately. 

It's not like I'm falling apart or anything, I don't want to make it sound worse than it is! It's just... well, I'm a choreographer, and the best way I can describe it is that it feels like the studio lights are on, but there’s just no music in me anymore. Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it okay.
Can you tell me if this feeling of sadness has affected your interest or enjoyment in activities, like choreographing or anything else you usually love doing?

Oh, um... I don't think so? I mean, I really hope not. I'm still going to the studio every day, and I still care about my work so much. I'd hate to let my dancers down, so I make sure I'm still doing everything I'm supposed to do. 

I wouldn't say I've lost interest at all, really. I'm still trying my absolute best to stay engaged and enjoy it, even if I feel a little heavy inside. Is it okay if I haven't noticed a change with that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information, and I definitely haven't stopped doing the things I love.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired or that you're lacking energy more often than usual, even if you're still doing your work and trying to stay engaged?

Um, well, maybe a little bit? I really don't want to sound lazy or anything, because I know everyone gets tired, and I'm really trying my best to push through it. 

But... I guess I have noticed that I feel pretty wiped out after doing just really small things lately. Like, um, just answering a single email to one of my dancers, or... or even just taking a shower, especially since I have this ankle brace on right now. It just takes it all out of me. And the frustrating part is, even if I go lie down to rest, it doesn't really recharge me. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just feel awful complaining about being tired, and I don't want you to think I'm not trying. Is it normal to feel that way?
Can you tell me if you’ve noticed a change in how much pleasure or joy you get from activities you usually enjoy, like choreographing or spending time with people you care about?

Um... I mean, I think I'm still getting joy out of it? I really try to focus on the positive parts of my day. I love my dancers, and I love seeing them perform, so I definitely still care about that. 

I guess... maybe it's just a little harder to feel that spark right now? Like, I'm still doing it, and I still want to be doing it, but the feeling of excitement isn't quite as loud as it usually is. But I wouldn't say I've lost the pleasure completely! I'm really trying to stay upbeat about it. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm ungrateful for my job or my friends. Is it okay that it just feels a little... muted right now?
Have you found yourself feeling more guilty or like you’re not good enough about things lately, even if you know logically that it might not make sense?

Um... well, I really try not to let myself think that way, because I know it doesn't help anything. I try to stay positive and focus on how to fix things, you know? 

But... I guess I have been struggling a little bit with... with feeling bad about the cancelled performances. I just keep replaying it in my head, and I can't help but feel like I completely let everyone down. The dancers worked so hard, and the funders... and the whole community, really. I just feel awful about it. 

I know I shouldn't be so hard on myself, especially because everyone has been so much kinder about it than I deserve. They've been really understanding. But I still just feel like I wasn't good enough to make it work. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just throwing a pity party for myself. Is it normal to feel that guilty about something like that, even when people tell you it's okay?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating more or less than usual or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Um... well, I haven't been trying to change my weight or anything, I promise. I always try to make sure I'm taking care of myself so I can be a good example for the dancers. 

But, um... I guess I have noticed my rehearsal clothes are hanging a little looser than usual lately? I feel bad even bringing it up, because I know I should be eating better. It's just... when I was having all those ideas and working so hard on the choreography before, I was just so focused that I'd kind of skip meals without really noticing? And now... I don't know, I try to eat, but food just sort of tastes like cardboard right now. 

I'm really trying to make myself eat more, though, I swear. I know it's important. I hope you don't think I'm doing it on purpose or being irresponsible with my health. Is it okay that my appetite is just a little off right now?
Have you noticed that you’ve been moving more slowly than usual or, on the contrary, that you feel restless or fidgety, like you can’t sit still?

Um... well, as a choreographer, I always try to stay really active and keep the energy up in the room. I don't want to bring anyone down or seem like I'm not giving it my all. 

But... I guess I have noticed I'm not quite as quick on my feet as I usually am? I feel a little embarrassed even admitting it, because I really don't want to seem lazy. But recently, even just doing something simple, like... crossing the studio to pick up my notebook, it just feels so slowed down. It's almost like my body is moving through wet sand instead of music, if that makes sense? 

I'm really trying to push through it, though, I promise. I keep trying to stretch and warm up like normal. I hope you don't think I'm just slacking off or not trying hard enough at work. Is it normal to feel that heavy and sluggish when you're going through a rough patch?
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like having trouble falling asleep, waking up too early, or sleeping much more than usual even if you don’t feel like you need to?

Um... well, I really try to keep a good schedule, you know? Sleep is so important for recovery, especially for dancers, and I always tell my team to make sure they're resting. I don't want to seem like I'm not practicing what I preach. 

But... I guess my sleep has been a little all over the place lately? I feel bad admitting it, because I know I should be managing it better. Like, before the performances were cancelled, I was just so inspired that I'd stay up sketching formations until dawn. I felt fine then, I promise, I was just really dedicated to the work. 

But lately... I don't know, I fall asleep completely exhausted, but then I just pop awake at four or five in the morning, and my stomach is just in knots. It's so tight. I really try to go back to sleep, I close my eyes and do deep breathing and everything, but I just can't. I hope you don't think I'm just having bad sleep hygiene or staying up looking at my phone or something. Is it okay that my sleep is a little messed up right now, with everything going on?
Have you noticed yourself feeling worse about who you are or feeling like you don’t measure up to the person you want to be lately?

Um... well, I really try to keep a positive mindset. As a choreographer, I know I need to be a strong role model and project confidence for the company. I'd hate for anyone to think I'm just wallowing or feeling sorry for myself, you know? 

But... I guess I have been struggling a little bit with feeling like I'm not... doing a good enough job? I feel awful even admitting it out loud, because everyone has been so incredibly supportive. It's just... I keep replaying the cancelled performances over and over in my head. I really try to just let it go and look forward, I promise, but I keep telling myself that I completely let everyone down. The dancers who worked so hard, the funders, the whole community... 

And honestly, people have been so much kinder about it than I actually deserve. They've been so sweet, which almost makes me feel worse, if that makes sense? I'm really trying hard to practice self-compassion and remind myself that some things are just out of my control. I don't want you to think I'm just throwing a pity party or not trying to move on. Do you think it's okay that I'm feeling a little guilty right now, just while we're trying to figure everything out?
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in things you usually enjoy, or that you can’t feel any pleasure from them anymore, even when you make yourself do them?

Um... well, I really try to keep doing the things I love, you know? I think it's so important to stay engaged and keep finding joy in the little things, especially when times are a bit tough. I don't want to be someone who just gives up on their passions.

But... honestly, I haven't completely lost interest in everything. I still try to listen to music, and I still love the *idea* of dance. I promise I'm still trying to do things that make me happy. It's just... maybe I don't get that same spark right now? Like, I'll put on a favorite track, and I know I *should* feel that rush to move, but it just feels a little flat at the moment. 

I'm still making the effort, though, I really am. I hope you don't think I'm just sitting around doing nothing all day. I know it's important to keep trying. Is it normal to just feel a little disconnected from your hobbies for a little while, as long as you're still trying?
Can you tell me if there have been days where nothing—not even things you usually love—has brought you any sense of pleasure or joy at all?

Um... no, not completely. I really want to be clear about that, because I don't want you to think I'm just totally shut down or not trying to find the good in my days. I know how important it is to keep a positive outlook.

I mean, I always try to find at least one little thing to appreciate every day, even if it's just a nice cup of tea or seeing the sun come through the window. I promise I haven't had days where there's just... absolutely nothing. It's more like I was saying before, where the joy is just a little dimmer right now. But I'm still feeling *something*, I really am. I wouldn't let myself just completely give up on finding pleasure in life, you know? That wouldn't be healthy at all. 

So, no, I wouldn't say there have been days with zero joy. I'm doing my best to keep my spirits up. Does that make sense? I hope that's a good sign that I'm still trying my best to stay engaged with everything.
Have you noticed that even when you make yourself do things you usually enjoy, like choreographing or spending time with friends, you don’t feel any pleasure from them anymore?

Um... well, like I mentioned, I really am trying my best to stay connected to the things I love. I don't want to sound like I'm just going through the motions and getting absolutely nothing out of it, because I know how important it is to keep trying. 

When I make myself work on some choreography or, you know, see friends, it's not like I feel completely numb or empty. I promise I'm not just sitting there feeling miserable. I still smile, and I still appreciate being around people who care about me. It's just... maybe the feeling isn't quite as big or as bright as it used to be? But I definitely wouldn't say I don't feel *any* pleasure anymore. 

I'm really making an effort to be present and enjoy those moments, even if it takes a little more energy right now. I hope you can see that I'm really trying to push through this and stay positive. Is it okay that I'm still doing these things even if the feeling isn't 100% there right now? I just want to make sure I'm handling this the right way.

Have there been times when even the things you usually care about the most, like choreographing or seeing your closest friends, have felt completely empty or meaningless to you, even when you're trying your hardest to engage with them?

Oh, gosh, no. Never meaningless. I mean... my friends are my rock, and dance is my whole life. I would never want you to think I don't value them anymore, or that I'm just totally checked out. 

Even if I'm having a slower week where things feel a bit muted, like we talked about, I still know exactly how much they matter to me. It's never felt empty. I really make sure to remind myself how lucky I am to have my friends and my career, even on the days when I have to push myself a little harder to get out the door. I would feel just awful if I ever let myself think of them as meaningless. 

I hope that shows I'm keeping a good perspective on things? I really don't want to come across as ungrateful or, you know, totally detached from my life, because I'm definitely not. I'm trying really hard to stay grounded in what's important. That's the right way to handle it, isn't it?
Would you say that you’ve been feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Um... well, I don't know if I would use the word depressed, just because that sounds so severe, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or just giving up. I promise I'm trying my hardest to keep a good attitude. 

But... I guess I have been feeling a bit down lately. What actually brought me in to see you is that, for the past couple of weeks, I’ve been waking up with this... this heavy, kind of hollow sadness. It’s a bit hard to explain, but it feels like... like the studio lights are on, but there’s just no music in me anymore. 

I'm still getting out of bed and trying to push through it every day, though! I really don't want you to think I'm just wallowing in it or letting it take over. It's just taking a little more effort to find my rhythm right now, and it tends to linger through the day. Is it normal to feel a little stuck like that sometimes? I just want to make sure I'm handling it the right way and not overreacting.
Have you ever felt so overwhelmed by how you're feeling that you've thought about hurting yourself or not wanting to live anymore?

Oh, no, no. I would never do that. I promise, it's really not that bad. I mean, yes, I've been feeling down, like I said, but I would never want to do anything to hurt myself. I know how much that would upset my friends and my family, and I could never put them through that. 

I really try to focus on the positive and just keep moving forward, even when it's hard. I want to get better and get back to feeling like myself again. I'm not the kind of person who just gives up. I'm handling this the right way by coming to see you and getting help, right? I really hope you don't think I'm in some kind of crisis, because I'm definitely safe and I want to be here.
Would you say that in the past two weeks, you’ve noticed a loss of pleasure in activities you usually enjoy, like choreographing or seeing friends, even when you make an effort to engage in them?

Oh, um... I know we touched on this a little bit a minute ago, but no, I really haven't lost the pleasure in them. I wouldn't say that at all. 

I mean, like I mentioned, with that heavy feeling lately, sometimes it takes a little more energy to actually get myself to the studio or to get ready to meet up with people. But once I'm actually there? I still love it. I really do. Choreographing still gives me that same spark, and seeing my friends still makes me smile. 

I always try to focus on the good parts of my day, and I make sure to really appreciate those moments when I'm doing what I love. I haven't lost that joy at all. I hope it doesn't seem like I'm just brushing off your questions, I just... I want to be completely honest that I still really enjoy the things I care about. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I'm still finding the joy in things?
Would you say that most of the time, even when you're doing things you usually enjoy, the pleasure feels significantly dulled or almost gone?

Um, well, like I was saying, I really don't think it's gone at all. I mean, I guess sometimes it might feel a tiny bit less... vibrant? Just because I'm feeling a bit tired or heavy, like I mentioned. 

But I promise I'm not sitting there feeling completely numb or anything. I'm still smiling and laughing with my friends, and I still feel that connection when I'm working on a routine. I really try to stay present and soak in the good moments, you know? I wouldn't say the pleasure is dulled, just... maybe it takes a second longer to warm up to it right now. But the joy is definitely still there. I'm doing the right thing by keeping up with my activities, right? I just want to make sure I'm staying on track.
Have you noticed any difficulty concentrating or thinking clearly lately, even when you're trying to focus on something important like your choreography?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, I think my concentration is pretty good. 

I guess sometimes, if I'm feeling really tired, my mind might wander just a tiny bit, but nothing major. I can always pull myself back to what I'm doing. When I'm in the studio working on a piece, I'm still really focused on the steps and the music. I definitely wouldn't say I'm having a hard time thinking clearly. 

I always make sure to double-check my work anyway, just to be safe. I'm really trying to stay on top of everything, even when I feel a little drained. That's normal, right? To just have a moment where you lose your train of thought when you're tired? I really don't think it's anything to worry about.
Would you say that most days, you’re not getting any real enjoyment out of things you usually love, even when you make yourself do them?

Um, no, definitely not. I know we keep circling back to this, but I really am still getting enjoyment out of things. 

I mean, I'm not forcing myself to do things just to go through the motions. When I'm at the studio or out with friends, I really am happy to be there. I'm still feeling the love for what I do. I wouldn't say my days are completely devoid of joy at all. 

I really am trying my best to stay positive and keep doing the things that make me happy. It's so important to keep doing what you love, right? I'm sure it's good that I'm still finding enjoyment in my days, even if I'm a little tired. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I'm doing.
Would you say that most days, you’re not getting any real enjoyment out of things you usually love, even when you make yourself do them?

I feel like we just talked about this, but um... no, I'm really not losing my enjoyment of things. I'm sorry if I wasn't clear before, I just... I really want to make sure you know I'm still feeling happy when I do the things I love. 

Like I said, I'm not just forcing myself through my routines or anything. When I'm dancing, I'm still feeling that spark, you know? I really am. I'm trying so hard to stay engaged and positive, and I think I'm doing a pretty good job of it. It's good that I'm still feeling that joy, right? I'm doing okay?

The patient continues to endorse symptoms such as anhedonia (muted pleasure), fatigue, guilt, appetite disturbance, psychomotor slowing, and early morning awakening, which support the presence of a moderate or severe depressive episode. There is no clear evidence of manic or hypomanic symptoms, ruling out bipolar disorder. No new information has emerged to exclude any of the previous candidates entirely, nor to confirm a single diagnosis definitively.
